title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: China tightens approvals for offshore listings by red-chip firms, threatening Hong Kong IPO market: Reuters
items.content_text: The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has informed law firms that red-chip companies established after the 2023 administrative measures for overseas securities offerings must relocate their place of incorporation to mainland China to receive approval for offshore listings. This policy signals a rigorous shift toward enforcing substantive domestic jurisdiction over overseas fundraising vehicles.

items.title: Ex-Alibaba Star’s AI Startup Doubles Valuation to $5 Billion
items.content_text: A generative AI startup founded by the former head of Alibaba Group's AI division has secured new funding, doubling its valuation to $5 billion within a few months. This capital injection underscores sustained investor confidence in the commercial viability of high-tier foundational model developers.

items.title: Signal to Restrict Screenshots to Block AI Agents, Urges Regulation on Apple, Google and Microsoft
items.content_text: Signal has introduced default screenshot restrictions to prevent OS-level AI agents, such as Apple Siri and Google Gemini, from scraping screen data and bypassing end-to-end encryption. The company stated that these agents pose a severe privacy threat by leveraging system-level permissions and has urged Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide more granular platform control tools.

items.title: Regular Tech Bros Are Worried About Honeypots
items.content_text: Executives and core engineers in Silicon Valley are increasingly vigilant against corporate espionage facilitated through romantic relationships. Business intelligence and high-end matchmaking firms report a surge in demand for comprehensive background checks, non-disclosure agreements, and behavioral audits as standard defensive measures against the leakage of sensitive intellectual property.

items.title: SK Hynix to Convert Kioxia Bond and Become Top Shareholder
items.content_text: SK Hynix is considering converting its holdings in Kioxia convertible bonds into equity. This move is intended to solidify SK Hynix's strategic position as the largest shareholder of the Japanese NAND flash manufacturer amidst semiconductor market volatility and a cooling AI investment cycle.

items.title: Hermes Agent's Collective Wisdom feature turns one employee's AI trick into the whole team's skill
items.content_text: AI research lab Nous Research has launched an enterprise version of Hermes Agent, integrated into Microsoft Teams and secured within Azure Container Apps sandboxes. The new 'Collective Wisdom' feature enables employees to convert successful automated workflows into team-wide shared assets, while ensuring that internal operational data is excluded from third-party model training.

items.title: AI Threatens to Make China’s Jobs Slump Much Worse
items.content_text: Gartner projects a net gain of 1.7 million jobs by 2030, with 10.6 million created against 8.9 million lost globally. Chief forecaster John Lovelock notes that firms are transitioning from 'deferred hiring' to productive deployment, expecting a rebound in labor demand as AI systems move past the Trough of Disillusionment.

items.title: Google is rolling out a collapsible sidebar on its desktop Search homepage, letting users easily find and resume recent AI searches (Barry Schwartz/Search Engine Roundtable)
items.content_text: Google has officially rolled out a collapsible sidebar on its desktop Search homepage, a strategic move by its search experience division to enhance continuity for users engaged in multi-turn AI queries. The feature is designed to shift search patterns from one-off interactions toward long-term engagement by providing a persistent hub for recent AI-generated tasks.

items.title: Singapore-Based DayOne Is Said to Pause US IPO Plans on Data Center, Market Concerns
items.content_text: Singapore-based DayOne Data Centers has shelved its planned US IPO amid cooling market valuations for AI infrastructure and intensifying regulatory scrutiny. Despite efforts to navigate the AI compute demand surge, the company faces significant headwinds from investor skepticism regarding data center asset sustainability and strict US regulations on the export of advanced AI hardware to entities with China-linked operations.

items.title: This 16-Year-Old Founded an AI Missile Startup. He’s Targeting ‘Cost per Kill’
items.content_text: At 16 years old, Henrijs Dandzbergs is too young to vote. Or drink. Or smoke. Or drive unsupervised. But he’s not too young to win half a million dollars for his AI-guided-missile startup. In September, Dandzbergs, who was born in Latvia, was admitted to Y Combinator’s fall 2026 cohort. The startup accelerator counts companies like Airbnb, Stripe, DoorDash, and Reddit among its alumni; Dandzbergs is likely the youngest solo founder in its vaunted history. items.title: Samsung names Choi Won-Joon head of its mobile division, replacing TM Roh, who stays as Samsung co-CEO, and Sang Joon Hwang to lead its memory business (Ben Schoon/9to5Google)
items.content_text: Samsung Electronics has announced a leadership transition in its MX (Mobile Experience) business unit, appointing Chief Operating Officer Choi Won-Joon as the new head of the mobile division to oversee post-Galaxy S26 and Z Fold 8 product strategy. TM Roh will step down from the mobile leadership role but will retain his position as Samsung Electronics co-CEO, focusing on broader corporate strategy and cross-divisional integration.

items.title: Nscale’s ByteDance Deal Faces Scrutiny Under US Chip Curbs
items.content_text: Nscale, a UK-based AI infrastructure provider, faces intense scrutiny from US export regulators during its IPO process due to its rental agreement providing Nvidia B200 GPU access to a ByteDance subsidiary in Singapore. The contract, which once accounted for 73% of Nscale's revenue, now sits at the center of a compliance crisis exacerbated by November 2026 export controls and revelations of the client's ties to US-blacklisted entities, threatening the company's financial transparency and listing prospects.

items.title: Industrial monitoring startup BrightAI closes $97M investment
items.content_text: BrightAI Inc., a startup that helps industrial companies detect malfunctioning equipment, has raised $97 million in funding. Smith Point Capital led the Series A round. BrightAI said in its Wednesday announcement of the deal that a number of other venture capital firms contributed as well. They were joined by GE Vernova Inc., an energy equipment company that emerged from the 2024 split-up of General Electric Co. items.title: Tech stocks fall as Anthropic IPO fails to reignite AI trade
items.content_text: Technology stocks in Asia fell on Friday as Anthropic’s record listing in New York rattled the region’s equity markets and failed to reverse losses from a deepening sell-off in AI companies. Shares of SoftBank, which holds a roughly 13 per cent stake in OpenAI, sank more than 15 per cent, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 index shed nearly 5 per cent. items.title: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.content_text: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia to assess whether the personal conduct of former CEO Jensen Huang facilitated the unauthorized transfer of advanced chip technologies or confidential intelligence to Chinese entities. The investigation focuses on potential violations of state securities laws and failure to adequately disclose material risks to investors.

items.title: Anthropic Slumps 5% Post-Market After Record $107.3 Billion IPO
items.content_text: AI developer Anthropic PBC saw its shares decline by approximately 5% in post-market trading following a record-breaking $107.3 billion IPO. The stock had previously gained 17% during its debut, reflecting strong investor appetite for the maker of Claude, though broader market volatility eventually weighed on its performance.

items.title: Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast says
items.content_text: Documents released by the U.S. House Foreign Affairs Committee reveal that the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) approved the export of over 879,000 AI chips to Chinese firms including Alibaba and Tencent as of May 2026, with some recipients flagged by the Department of Defense as Chinese Military Companies. While Nvidia and AMD assert compliance with export control laws, Representative Gregory Meeks criticized the administration's enforcement efficacy, prompting congressional oversight into current regulatory policies.

items.title: Trump ousts cyber director after tech outages spark criticism
items.content_text: President Donald Trump dismissed National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross, with DoD CIO Kirsten Davies serving as interim lead. The move follows widespread technical outages that crippled U.S. air travel and banking sectors, prompting intense legislative scrutiny over the administration's crisis response capabilities.

items.title: What comes after AGI? From AGI to Superintelligence
items.content_text: For decades, AI research has been focused on a monumental milestone: building artificial general intelligence, or AGI - machines that match humans across nearly all cognitive tasks. It was always clear that, in principle, intelligence could progress beyond human level, but the prospect of AGI was far enough off, and surrounded by ample uncertainties of its own, that looking past it felt premature. items.title: The Big VC Winners In Anthropic’s IPO: Iconiq, Lightspeed And Others
items.content_text: Iconiq Capital has made a significant strategic investment exceeding $6 billion in AI startup Anthropic, with its roughly 1.8% equity stake now valued at approximately $31.8 billion. This surge occurs as Anthropic prepares for a landmark IPO, highlighting the massive capital deployment and high-leverage competition within the foundational model and AI ecosystem.

items.title: Anthropic’s US$1.5 trillion debut rewrites venture capital’s playbook
items.content_text: AI lab Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq on November 19 at an $83 IPO price, closing at $97.17 with a fully diluted valuation of $1.8 trillion. This liquidity event yields massive returns for early backers like Menlo Ventures and Spark Capital, signaling a structural shift in AI venture capital toward large-scale SPV-driven funding models.

items.title: Sources: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire diffusion LLM developer Inception for $500M+ plus earnouts; talks began before Jensen Huang's resignation (The Information)
items.content_text: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire diffusion-based LLM developer Inception for over $500 million, including earnouts. Inception recently launched Mercury 3, a model utilizing diffusion scaling laws to outperform autoregressive models like GPT-6.1-Sol in specific benchmarks, achieving speeds exceeding 1,000 tokens per second.

items.title: Sources: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving now to let the White House get a successor confirmed before Democrats take the Senate in January (Axios)
items.content_text: US National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is stepping down to provide a transition window for his successor to be confirmed by the Senate before Democrats gain control in January. As the head of the Office of the National Cyber Director, Cairncross led federal cybersecurity strategy and notably directed technical reviews of AI firms like Anthropic following commerce-led export control implementations.

items.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
items.content_text: Apple is pivoting its AI strategy by recruiting for a 'Proactive, Agentic AI' engineering lead to develop autonomous systems capable of cross-app interaction, code debugging, and complex task planning. The initiative, integrating teams from Siri, UI Frameworks, and Apple Foundation Models, aims to move beyond static voice commands toward an autonomous agent environment capable of multi-step execution across devices.

items.title: Apple Is Working on AI Agent for Device Control, Apps, Browsing and Coding
items.content_text: Bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of users. items.title: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
items.content_text: Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang resigned following misconduct allegations, causing the stock to drop nearly 40% from its October 6th peak, despite a record-breaking Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion and the rapid shipment of the Vera Rubin platform. Chairman Harvey Jones has confirmed that the board will not reinstate Huang and has initiated an executive search to stabilize leadership.

items.title: What’s With All These Outages?
items.content_text: Major infrastructure outages occurred sequentially at Microsoft, the FAA, JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, the NSA, and Apple. Despite official denials of cyberattacks, market anxiety is mounting due to the convergence of these failures with Anthropic's reported $1.5 trillion IPO plans, the first Nvidia earnings report post-Jensen Huang's resignation, and new US executive orders aimed at restricting Chinese entities from accessing AI compute via cloud rentals.

items.title: Intuit to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion
items.content_text: Intuit has reached an agreement to sell its email-marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock, slated for closure in early 2027. This divestiture, representing a loss of over 70% from the $12 billion acquisition price in 2021, follows Mailchimp's stagnant revenue growth and its role as a drag on Intuit's broader financial valuation.

items.title: At a Senate hearing, Trump's CISA director nominee Michael LoSapio dodged questions about the agency's priorities, denied January 6 was an attack, and more (Eric Geller/Cybersecurity Dive)
items.content_text: Michael LoSapio, CISO of Palantir and Trump’s nominee for CISA director, faced significant scrutiny during his Senate Homeland Security Committee confirmation hearing. He evaded questions regarding the administration’s budget cuts to CISA and denied the nature of the January 6, 2021 Capitol attack, raising alarms among lawmakers about his political alignment and commitment to agency autonomy.

items.title: The Jensen Huang Blast Radius Has Hit His Favorite Restaurants
items.content_text: Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia following allegations of multiple extramarital affairs. The incident has triggered widespread public scrutiny, with small businesses in Taipei weighing the reputational impact of their past association with him against the marketing value of his high-profile visits.
